Lara et al. - 2025 - A 20 m spatial reso:
**What it does:** This study develops a wall-to-wall 20 m spatial resolution peatland extent map covering approximately 1.5 million km² of Alaska, addressing the limitation of existing coarse 1 km² resolution peatland products by leveraging multi-source remote sensing data and ground observations.

**Key findings:** The map estimates that 7.3% (110,133 km²) of Alaska's terrestrial land area is peatland, with coverage varying across ecoregions (4.6% polar, 10.4% boreal, 5.3% maritime), and achieves an overall agreement of 85% validated against 2,785 reference points. Wet and moist peatlands compose 2.6% and 4.7% of terrestrial land area, respectively, with their ratio varying across ecoregions. The map successfully captured fine-scale peatland features, though performance was slightly limited in areas of high-density woody vegetation due to C-band SAR canopy penetration constraints.

**Methods:** A support vector machine classifier was trained on fused Sentinel-1 dual-polarization SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, and ArcticDEM morphometric derivatives, spatially constrained by a topographic cost-function-based peatland suitability model, using peat cores and ground observations as training and validation data.
